title: Teeth and their supporting tissues
intro: Teeth cut and grind food and contribute to speech and appearance. They are held by a living support system called the periodontium. A painless tooth is not necessarily healthy, and gum disease may progress before obvious looseness.

sections.heading: Layers of a tooth
paragraphs: The crown is covered by hard enamel; dentin lies beneath. Inside, the pulp contains nerves and blood vessels. Root surfaces have cementum rather than enamel, so gum recession exposes a different surface and can cause sensitivity.

sections.heading: How teeth are anchored
paragraphs: The periodontal ligament connects the root to surrounding bone and cushions load. Gums help seal and protect this attachment. Teeth are not simply glued into solid bone, and damage to support can occur separately from a cavity.

sections.heading: Plaque and damage
paragraphs: Bacterial plaque can cause decay or gum inflammation. Persistent inflammation may damage attachment and bone. Bleeding is a reason to improve suitable care and seek advice, not a reason to stop all cleaning.

sections.heading: Everyday protection
paragraphs: Brush gently with fluoride toothpaste and clean between teeth with suitable tools. Limit frequent sugary snacks and ask about dry mouth, smoking or diabetes. Dental visits should assess both teeth and gums; whitening does not treat decay or periodontitis.

sections.heading: When care is urgent
paragraphs: Persistent pain, swelling, a broken tooth or loose adult tooth needs assessment. Facial swelling with fever needs urgent dental advice; difficulty breathing or swallowing is an emergency. A knocked-out adult tooth is time-sensitive, while a baby tooth should not be put back. Before a consultation, note when a symptom began, what makes it better or worse, and how it affects ordinary activities. Bring previous reports if available. Ask the professional to connect the explanation to your own findings rather than assuming that a general description establishes a diagnosis.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira has bleeding gums without toothache. She books a dental visit and learns interdental cleaning rather than assuming painless means healthy.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben notices sensitivity at a receded gumline. A dentist checks exposed root and other causes before he buys repeated whitening treatments.
